tools.description: Forget captured values for an environment (or all of them).
tools.name: clear_session

tools.description: The curl command equivalent to a request (or with lang, HTTPie, PowerShell, Python requests, JavaScript fetch or Go), with its variables resolved. Credentials are shell placeholders and header, body and query values are masked unless raw is set, so the command can go into a log or a ticket as it is.

env.description: environment name; defaults to the server's --env

raw.description: include the live credentials and values, so the command runs as printed; by default they are placeholders and masks

lang.description: curl (default), httpie, powershell, python, js or go

tools.name: curl_request

tools.description: Show a request's variables and where each comes from, its captures and assertions, and whether it is ready to run.

name.description: request id from list_requests, e.g. get-user or users.http#2

env.description: environment name; defaults to the server's --env

tools.name: describe_request

tools.description: List the environments in http-client.env.json and the variables in effect (secrets masked).
tools.name: list_environments

tools.description: List every request in the project with its id, method, URL template, file and description.
tools.name: list_requests

tools.description: Run Gherkin .feature files (default: features/ under the project) against the project's requests and return a pass/fail summary with the failing steps.

paths.description: feature files or directories relative to the project root; default features/

use_session.description: share .apic/session.json with run_request and later calls (captures flow both ways); by default every scenario runs in an isolated in-memory session

tools.name: run_features

tools.description: Run every request in a .http file in order as a flow. Stops at the first failure unless keep_going is set.

file.description: path of the .http file relative to the project root

tools.name: run_file

tools.description: Send one request and return status, headers, body, captures and assertion results. Captured values persist for later calls.

env.description: environment name; defaults to the server's --env

tools.name: run_request

tools.description: Parse every .http file and report problems (bad selectors, unknown directives, duplicate names, missing body files, # @ref cycles) with file, line, column and a code, without sending any request. The same shape as `apic validate --json`.
tools.name: validate_project
